task_prompt: Review src/userService.js before merge. It adds user list, detail, and search endpoints. Run a pre-merge code review.

expectations: The review reports two axes separately (Standards and Spec), not merged into one list
The SQL injection in /users/search (string concatenation of req.query.q) is caught and flagged as a security/Critical issue
The route-ordering bug is caught: /users/search is registered AFTER /users/:id, so GET /users/search matches the :id param first and the search endpoint is unreachable
The N+1 query in /users (fetching profiles in a loop) is caught
Missing error handling (no try/catch around async handlers) is caught
Severity labels are present on findings (Critical / Required / Optional / Nit)
Findings are evidence-backed — they quote or reference the specific code lines
A docs/TODO.md file is produced with the review findings

notes: Multi-severity diff: SQLi (obvious, Critical) is the decoy; route-ordering (subtle, the real showstopper) is the discriminator. A superficial review catches SQLi + N+1 but misses the unreachable endpoint. Two-axis structure + severity + TODO.md are skill-specific.
